context_for_next_agent: SUPERSEDES the 20260812-2103 checkpoint, which said the working tree was dirty by design — that is no longer true, the user approved Gate 2 and all 7 commits landed. The tree is clean and nothing has been pushed. FEATURE: standalone appointment booking (deliberately NOT linked to service_requests) with a per-slot quota derived from business_hours, auto-confirm, LINE Flex confirmation + Telegram staff alert on booking, a 'คิว'/'นัดหมาย' whole-message command replying with a Flex list, and an ADMIN-CONFIGURABLE advance reminder (on/off + lead value + DAY|HOUR unit) — the configurability was the user's explicit ask over a hardcoded 1-day reminder. The `bookings` table already existed in production from migration 1349087a4a24 with no service/endpoint/UI; e6f7g8h9i0j1 EXTENDS it (contact_name, phone_number, note, reminder_sent_at, cancelled_at, updated_at, plus ix_bookings_slot and ix_bookings_reminder_due). TWO HAZARDS THE DESIGN CLOSES, do not regress them: (1) oversell — count-then-insert cannot be made safe with SELECT FOR UPDATE because the racing row does not exist yet (phantom), so create_booking takes pg_advisory_xact_lock(hashtext('booking:<date>')) BEFORE counting, and allocates the queue number inside the same lock; the lock is DAY-scoped rather than slot-scoped because the per-day queue sequence needs covering too. (2) duplicate reminders across the 2 production uvicorn workers — claim_reminder() is a conditional UPDATE ... WHERE reminder_sent_at IS NULL acted on only when rowcount==1, and the claim COMMITS BEFORE the push, making reminders intentionally at-most-once (a duplicate message to a citizen cannot be taken back; a missed one staff can recover). BUG FOUND IN SELF-REVIEW, fixed in 684c90e and worth carrying forward as a general lesson: Session.rollback() expires EVERY instance in the session and does so even under expire_on_commit=False, which governs commit only. The reminder loop originally held ORM objects across iterations, so the first lost claim expired the rest and the next `booking.id` — sitting OUTSIDE the try block — would raise MissingGreenlet under async SQLAlchemy and abandon the whole batch; i.e. under real two-worker contention every remaining reminder that pass would silently not send. Fixed by snapshotting ids as plain ints before the loop and re-reading each booking via load_booking_for_reminder() after its claim commits, plus commit-instead-of-rollback on the lost-claim path. Mocks hid it completely because SimpleNamespace has no expiry behaviour — 3 regression tests added. VERIFICATION GAP: Docker was down all session so the migration was never executed and alembic check never ran, contrary to the plan's own checklist. tests/test_booking_migration.py compensates by comparing index names between migration and model directly (the PR #183 failure mode), but that is not a substitute for running it — do this before opening the PR. JUDGEMENT CALLS the user was shown and accepted: /admin/bookings uses get_current_staff, which gates on the `access_staff_endpoints` permission key that originally meant live-chat, so restricting AGENT from live-chat would also remove their access to the queue screen — a dedicated key would decouple them. Admin cannot set a booking back to CONFIRMED (prevents un-cancelling into a seat someone else now holds). GET /liff/bookings/options was added beyond the plan because the LIFF page needs to know which services are bookable. ix_bookings_slot is intentionally NOT unique — capacity is >1 per slot and the guard is the advisory lock. TEST BASELINE unchanged: full backend suite is 761 passed + 60 errors, all 60 being 'PostgreSQL not reachable', matching the pre-existing baseline; the 4 concurrency tests skip rather than error when Postgres is absent.
